questions.question: What is tourism trend analysis? / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• What is tourism trend analysis?. (2 marks) Systematic study of changes/patterns in tourism
  • over time - Uses tourist data and behaviour/preferences to identify trends and support
  • planning/forecasting (1+1)

questions.question: What is meant by tourism trends analysis? / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• What is meant by tourism trends analysis?. (2 marks) Collecting and examining tourism -
  • related information to identify patterns, changes and emerging developments - May compare
  • periods, destinations, tourist groups or preferences to interpret likely future direction (1+1)

questions.question: What is social media analysis in tourism? / [CO4]

questions.question: Explain the emerging trend of spiritual and pilgrimage tourism in India. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Emerging trend of spiritual and pilgrimage tourism in India. (5 marks) Meaning: travel
  • for religious, spiritual or faith-based purposes (1) - Examples: Varanasi, Ayodhya, Tirupati, Char
  • Dham, Bodh Gaya, major church/mosque/pilgrimage centres (1) - Growth factors: faith, heritage
  • interest, improved access, promotion and digital booking/information (1) - Tourism benefits:
  • local jobs, transport, accommodation, guiding, crafts and small businesses (1) -
  • Issues/management: crowding, waste, carrying capacity, safety and protection of sacred sites;
  • sustainable management (1)
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Discuss the major emerging tourism trends and their relevance to contemporary tourism. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Major emerging tourism trends and relevance to contemporary tourism. (5 marks)
  • Identify relevant trends: sustainable/responsible, wellness, experiential/local,
  • adventure/ecotourism, medical, rural, solo/Gen Z, MICE or spiritual tourism (2) - Digital trends:
  • social media, online travel agencies, mobile booking and AI personalisation (1) - Reflect
  • changing preferences for authentic, flexible, convenient and meaningful experiences (1) -
  • Relevance: product innovation, destination marketing, competitiveness, employment and
  • sustainability (1)
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Explain how empirical analysis can be used to understand tourist behaviour and tourism trends. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Use of empirical analysis to understand tourist behaviour and tourism trends. (5
  • marks) Empirical analysis uses observed/measured evidence rather than assumptions (1) -
  • Collect primary data: surveys, interviews, observation, focus groups; secondary data: arrival
  • statistics, booking records, reviews and reports (1) - Analyse expenditure, length of stay,
  • purpose, satisfaction, origin and preferences using averages, percentages, comparisons or graphs
  • (1) - Compare groups, destinations or years to reveal patterns and changes (1) - Use findings for
  • planning, segmentation, product development, marketing and forecasting (1)
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Explain how measures of central tendency can be used to analyse tourist expenditure or length of stay. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Measures of central tendency for tourist expenditure or length of stay. (5 marks) Mean:
  • total expenditure/total nights divided by number of tourists/visits; shows average (2) - Median:
  • middle value after arranging observations; useful when extreme spending or long stays distort
  • the mean (1.5) - Mode: most frequently occurring expenditure value or length of stay (1) -
  • Application: compare visitor groups/destinations and support pricing, package design and
  • planning (0.5)
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Discuss the major challenges in analysing tourist behaviour and travel patterns. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Major challenges in analysing tourist behaviour and travel patterns. (5 marks)
  • Incomplete, unreliable or inconsistent data and under -reporting (1) - Different definitions,
  • collection methods and reporting periods (1) - Tourist preferences change rapidly due to trends,
  • income, technology, crises and social media (1) - Seasonality, diverse visitor groups and
  • difficulty representing all tourists (1) - Privacy/ethical concerns, limited resources and difficulty
  • interpreting online data; triangulate sources and update data (1)
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Explain the importance of sustainability in the development of wellness and retreat tourism. / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Importance of sustainability in wellness and retreat tourism. (5 marks) Protects natural
  • landscapes, water, biodiversity and the peaceful setting on which retreats depend (1) - Reduces
  • waste, pollution, energy use and pressure on local resources (1) - Supports local employment,
  • community participation, local food and cultural respect (1) - Maintains authentic, safe and high-
  • quality wellness experiences over the long term (1) - Promotes responsible visitor numbers, eco-
  • friendly facilities and monitoring/certification where appropriate (1)
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Explain the role of observation in analysing local tourism experiences. / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Role of observation in analysing local tourism experiences. (5 marks) Directly watches
  • tourist activities, interactions and use of local places/services (1) - Records behaviour, visitor
  • flows, waiting times, service quality, accessibility and environmental impacts (1) - Can be
  • structured using checklists/field notes and repeated at different times/seasons (1) - Reveals
  • details tourists may not mention in surveys; helps assess authenticity and experience quality (1) -
  • Limitations: observer bias, limited time and privacy; combine with interviews, surveys and
  • reviews (1)
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Explain the importance of sentiment analysis in understanding tourist opinions and preferences. / [CO4] [5x5 = 25]
questions.solution_html:
• Importance of sentiment analysis in understanding tourist opinions and preferences. (5
  • marks) Analyses text in reviews, comments and social posts to classify opinions as positive,
  • negative or neutral (1) - Identifies satisfaction, complaints, expectations and preferred features
  • (1) - Detects recurring themes such as service, price, cleanliness, safety, transport or attractions
  • (1) - Helps destinations/businesses improve services, marketing and reputation management (1) -
  • Limitations: sarcasm, language, fake reviews, bias and privacy; interpret with context and other
  • data (1)

questions.question: Analyse the impact of digitalisation, social media, online travel agencies and artificial intelligence on the progress of Indian tourism. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Impact of digitalisation, social media, OTAs and AI on the progress of Indian tourism.
  • (15 marks) Introduction: digital tools have changed how tourists search, compare, book,
  • experience and review travel (1) - Digitalisation: websites, mobile apps, digital payments, e -
  • tickets and online information improve access, convenience and efficiency (2) - Social media:
  • images, videos, influencers, hashtags and user -generated content create destination awareness
  • and influence choices; reviews spread quickly (2) - Online travel agencies (OTAs): compare
  • prices/options, enable booking of flights, hotels and packages , widen market reach and support
  • small providers; commissions and platform dependence are challenges (2) - Artificial
  • intelligence: chatbots, personalised recommendations, demand forecasting, sentiment analysis,
  • dynamic pricing and customer support (2) - Impact on Indian tourism: wider
  • domestic/international reach, easier trip planning, new business opportunities, better data -led
  • decisions and support for lesser -known destinations (2) - Challenges: digital divide,
  • inaccurate/fake information, privacy and cybersecurity, algorithmic bias, platform costs and
  • reduced human interaction (2) - Conclusion: combine technology with reliable information,
  • digital skills, inclusive access and responsible/sustainable destination management (2)
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Explain measures of central tendency and discuss their applications in tourism data analysis. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Measures of central tendency and their applications in tourism data analysis. (15
  • marks) Introduction/meaning: central tendency summarises a dataset using a representative
  • central value (1) - Mean: sum of all observations divided by number of observations; explain
  • formula or calculation (3) - Median: middle value after arranging data; for an even number,
  • average the two middle values; useful for skewed data/outliers (3) - Mode: most frequently
  • occurring value; useful for common package price, stay duration or visitor preference categories
  • where applicable (2) - Tourism applications: average tourist expenditure, length of stay, daily
  • spending, room rate, visitor numbers or satisfaction scores (2) - Interpretation/use: compare
  • destinations, seasons and visitor segments; support pricing, budgeting, marketing and planning
  • (2) - Limitations: mean is affected by extreme values; median ignores many individual values;
  • mode may be absent/multiple; measures alone do not show variation or explain causes (2)
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Explain how tourist feedback, online reviews and social media data can be used to identify emerging local tourism experience trends. / [CO4] [15x1 = 15]
questions.solution_html:
• Using tourist feedback, online reviews and social media data to identify emerging local
  • tourism experience trends. (15 marks) Introduction: online and direct feedback provide
  • evidence of visitor needs, perceptions and changing interests (1) - Sources: questionnaires,
  • interviews, review platforms, ratings, comments, hashtags, posts, photos, videos and
  • search/booking data (2) - Collection and preparation: define destination/time period, gather
  • relevant data, remove duplicates/spam where possible, protect privacy and organise themes (2) -
  • Methods: review coding, frequency counts, ratings, sentiment analysis, keyword/hashtag
  • analysis, observation and comparison over time (3) - Identify trends: local food, culture and
  • crafts, community -led activities, nature/adventure, wellness, authentic experiences or less -
  • crowded places, where supported by the data (2) - Interpretation: compare seasons, visitor
  • segments and positive/negative feedback; triangulate online data with surveys, observation and
  • stakeholder views (2) - Applications: improve products and service quality, support local
  • businesses, target marketing, manage visitor flows and guide sustainable planning (2) -
  • Limitations/conclusion: online users may not represent all tourists; fake reviews, language, bias
  • and changing platforms affect reliability; use ethical, balanced and regularly updated analysis (1)
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026
